mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or if Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence rise.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of falling unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or if Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP by more than 1% in the last quarter signals a strong demand environment, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong GDP growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or if Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in the last two months signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic output slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of falling industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or if Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strong demand environment, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong housing starts and consumption compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or if Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 in the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong payroll growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or if Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index by more than 0.5% in the last two months signals a disinflationary environment, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real purchasing power increases.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of falling CPI compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or if Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP and a decrease in the unemployment rate signals a robust economic environment, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as both consumer and business confidence rise.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong GDP growth and falling unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or if Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
